rule: GOAL: Move the single block from its starting square to the marked target zone. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the entire board, sliding all contents in that direction until they hit a wall or obstacle. RULE: The block only moves when pushed by the board's edge; it never stops mid-slide on its own. TRAP: Believing you can stop the block at a specific spot without using walls as brakes wastes many turns.

GOAL: Move the block to the marked square using only pushes. CONTROLS: Arrows shift your position; space pushes the adjacent block one step. RULE: You cannot pull blocks, so plan paths that allow forward momentum. TRAP: Assuming you can walk through gaps without pushing first wastes turns.

GOAL: Move the player to the exit tile using minimal steps. CONTROLS: Arrows shift position; Space confirms the final move. RULE: Each action counts, so plan a straight path without backtracking. TRAP: Assuming you can skip the confirmation step wastes actions and resets progress.

GOAL: Move the player to the exit tile without triggering any hidden traps. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shifted position one step; spacebar revealed adjacent tiles safely. RULE: Only revealed tiles are safe to enter, forcing cautious exploration before movement. TRAP: Assuming all visible floor was solid led to fatal steps into hidden pits.

GOAL: Guide the robot to the exit by navigating a shifting maze. CONTROLS: Arrows move the robot; space activates a temporary bridge. RULE: Bridges only form on tiles adjacent to walls and vanish after one step. TRAP: Believing bridges persist allowed you to plan long paths that collapsed mid-travel, wasting actions.

GOAL: Reach the exit tile before running out of moves. CONTROLS: Arrows moved your character one step; space activated switches or doors. RULE: Every switch toggles all connected gates, so order matters more than speed. TRAP: Assuming a door stays open after you pass through it wastes turns when you must return.

GOAL: Move two pieces to target zones while a wall reflects their positions. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the selected object; Space cycles selection between pieces and the wall. RULE: The wall acts as a mirror, so moving it changes where reflections appear relative to the pieces. TRAP: Assuming pieces move independently of the wall’s position wastes actions; you must align the reflection axis first.

ESTABLISHED: Blue is the player. Yellow, Gray, and Green are static blocks. The grid is 64x64. FAILED: Covering all three blocks sequentially. Returning to start after coverage. Moving without touching blocks. GOAL IS NOT: Simply covering the blocks or returning to the origin point. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the blue block one cell per press.

GOAL: Reach the exit door by navigating a simple grid without obstacles. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved your character one square in that direction. RULE: You must step directly onto the door tile to complete the level. TRAP: Believing you needed to collect items or press a button, when only movement mattered.

GOAL: Guide the glowing orb to the exit door without touching any walls. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the orb one step in that direction. RULE: The orb only moves if the path is clear; blocked paths cause no movement but still count as an action. TRAP: Assuming diagonal movement was possible, wasting actions trying to cut corners instead of following the straight corridors.

GOAL: Align all four colored tiles to match the target pattern shown on the screen. CONTROLS: Press arrow keys to slide the entire grid one step in that direction, wrapping around edges. RULE: Tiles move together as a single unit; you cannot shift individual pieces independently. TRAP: Believing you could isolate a specific color by moving only it, which is impossible since the whole board shifts simultaneously.

GOAL: Move the block to the marked square using only ten precise steps. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift your position one tile at a time in four directions. RULE: Every single movement counts toward the limit, so plan the shortest path before starting. TRAP: Assuming you can undo moves or take detours wastes actions and breaks the strict count.

GOAL: Clear the level by removing all obstacles. CONTROLS: Left-click selects items; right-click confirms removal. RULE: Only adjacent pairs can be removed together. TRAP: Believing any two matching items could be paired regardless of position wasted moves.

GOAL: Align the three scattered fragments to form a single, unbroken circle. CONTROLS: Left-click selects a piece; right-click rotates it clockwise by ninety degrees. RULE: Pieces only snap together when their curved edges match perfectly without gaps. TRAP: Assuming you could drag pieces freely; they actually lock into place once aligned.

GOAL: Merge two balls into a single cell. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move both balls simultaneously in the chosen direction. RULE: Balls stop when hitting walls, obstacles, or hazards. TRAP: Thinking balls can pass through each other or hazards; they cannot.

ESTABLISHED: The socket at the start triggers a rewind. The ghost replays your initial path. The bottom row is clear floor leading to the target. FAILED: Moving directly to the target while the piston is active. The piston blocks the only vertical shortcut. GOAL IS NOT: Simply standing on the socket. It is a mechanism, not the finish line. CONTROLS: Arrows move you. Space activates the socket, resetting your position and starting the ghost replay.

GOAL: Reach the glowing target tile. CONTROLS: Arrows move. Space activates the time-ghost to replay your path. RULE: The ghost repeats your exact movements, allowing you to pass through or push objects it interacts with. TRAP: Believing you must stay put while the ghost works; instead, move immediately after activation to sync your position for the next phase.

GOAL: Move two shapes to cover colored dots and paint them the matching hue. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active shape; Space switches to the next shape. RULE: A shape changes color only when its tip touches a colored square. TRAP: Thinking color persists if you leave the square; the last contact wins, so end on the target color.

GOAL: Position Yellow and Orange tiles inside their matching colored brackets. CONTROLS: Rotate the left circle clockwise or counter-clockwise, or rotate the right circle clockwise or counter-clockwise. RULE: Each rotation shifts tiles along that specific circle; tiles at shared cells move according to the circle being rotated. TRAP: Assuming you must track every tile’s position; only Yellow and Orange matter, as other tiles do not affect their paths.

GOAL: Seat four scattered tokens into their matching floor rings. CONTROLS: Click a token to select it, then use arrow keys to slide it until it stops or hits a wall. RULE: Tokens only settle when perfectly aligned with a ring; partial overlaps are invalid. TRAP: Assuming a token stops immediately; it slides freely until blocked, so overshooting is common.

GOAL: Match the hidden pattern by setting the correct tiles to white, treating gray preview cells as background to be ignored. CONTROLS: Click a tile to toggle its color between white and gray. RULE: Gray preview tiles act as wildcards, meaning those specific board positions do not need to match the preview exactly. TRAP: Assuming gray preview cells require the board to be gray, which caused unnecessary toggling and wasted moves.

GOAL: Move the yellow and orange tokens to specific target cells on the grid. CONTROLS: Left and right arrows shifted the horizontal track; up and down arrows shifted the vertical track. RULE: The board consists of two crossing loops; moving one track shifts all tokens on it, including those at intersections. TRAP: Assuming arrows act only on their specific corner; they actually rotate the entire global horizontal or vertical path.

GOAL: Identify the hidden color for overlapping grid regions and paint all matching cells correctly. CONTROLS: Click a cell to cycle its color from blue to red to orange. RULE: Overlapping regions must share one consistent color, forcing the hidden value to be red. TRAP: Assuming one click sets any color; cells needing orange required two clicks to cycle past red.

GOAL: Place yellow tiles into the two bracket cells at the ends of the top row. CONTROLS: Top arrows rotate the top row; side arrows rotate the large loop connecting the rest of the board. RULE: The two rotation paths share the top row cells, allowing you to move tiles between the loop and the top row. TRAP: Thinking you must rotate the large loop to align the top row; use top arrows for quick adjustments there.

GOAL: Move the plug into the socket. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plug three spaces; Space rotates it. RULE: The plug must align perfectly with the socket's prongs. TRAP: Assuming Space costs a move; rotation is free, so use it to orient correctly before sliding.

GOAL: Align the black piece’s mirror reflection exactly over the yellow target. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide the piece three cells per press. RULE: The game only ends when the reflection perfectly overlaps the target. TRAP: Assuming the piece moves one cell or wraps around the edge.

GOAL: Align the plug's yellow prong with the wall's yellow gap. CONTROLS: Click the bottom blue button to move the plug left. RULE: Each click shifts the plug by a fixed distance until alignment is perfect. TRAP: Assuming the gray shadow indicated the correct path instead of the color match.

GOAL: Navigate the grid to reach the green tile from the start. CONTROLS: Arrow keys swap the player with the adjacent tile, moving one step. RULE: Movement is only possible through open doors; walls block passage completely. TRAP: Assuming walls shift or doors change; they are static, so plan the path before moving.

ESTABLISHED: Green is safe at the blue block. The red bar and blue block are toggleable only if the green stands clear. FAILED: Moving the green before toggling the blue block seals the exit path or kills the green. GOAL IS NOT: Simply walking to the yellow target; the layout must change first. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the green two cells. Clicking red or blue toggles their state, but kills the green if it is standing on them.

GOAL: Align the plug with the wall gap by managing gray fluid flow between bands. CONTROLS: Click top buttons to pump gray up, clearing middle band space; click side button to move plug right. RULE: Gray flows upward when space opens above, creating room below for the plug to advance. TRAP: Moving the plug without first clearing the middle band causes immediate blockage.

GOAL: Move the plug down to land precisely in the socket. CONTROLS: Click vertical stems to set them dark; click the blob to run. RULE: Each dark stem lowers the plug one step; all five must be dark. TRAP: Thinking horizontal bars affect movement; they are visual hints only.

GOAL: Cover the yellow zone using the mirrored piece. CONTROLS: Arrows move the dotted object; Space swaps the active object between the piece and its mirror. RULE: Only the object marked with dots responds to directional input. TRAP: Assuming arrows always control the main piece, ignoring that the dot pattern dictates which side you are driving.

GOAL: Fill every gray socket with a matching plug. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate and move the unit; Space grabs or releases the attached block. RULE: A plug only fits when its prongs perfectly align with the socket’s shape. TRAP: Assuming centering the block was enough; precise orientation and offset mattered more than position.

GOAL: Match each bottom blue shape to its paired pink shape using the top legend. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor between slots; DOWN cycles the shape choice. RULE: The top pairs define a fixed, arbitrary mapping between blue and pink shapes. TRAP: Assuming a geometric transformation rule wastes time; the pairing is purely associative.

GOAL: Reach the exit while safely navigating past a lethal, lunging socket hazard. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the plug one room per press. RULE: The socket is deadly only from its prong side; enter from perpendicular directions to survive. TRAP: Assuming the socket is an obstacle to be avoided entirely rather than a directional hazard to be approached safely.

GOAL: Clear three green blocks to open a ceiling passage, then rise into the upper room to reach the pink target. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player horizontally; clicking blocks clears them. RULE: The player rises automatically only when fully aligned under the cleared opening. TRAP: Clicking blocks before moving into position fails to trigger the ascent; you must align after clearing.

GOAL: Fill the top half white and bottom half purple to match the preview. CONTROLS: Mouse selects color; Space stamps the rotated shape; arrows rotate the stamp orientation. RULE: Rotating the stamp flips which half it paints; the upright position covers only the top rows. TRAP: Assuming up/down arrows rotate the stamp at the inverted position, when they actually do nothing.

GOAL: Guide the green token to the yellow goal box. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the token; clicks activate red and blue buttons to change maze paths. RULE: You must press the colored buttons to open the correct doors before your token can reach the exit. TRAP: Assuming the health bar is a strict action limit; it does not kill you, allowing extra exploration without penalty.

GOAL: Reach the green marker while navigating rooms with dangerous prongs. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one room per press. RULE: Entering a socket room consumes it, but standing in its adjacent prong room kills you instantly. TRAP: Assuming prongs attack along entire rows; they only strike the single adjacent room, so timing entry to consume sockets is key.

GOAL: Place two distinct pieces onto separate colored targets without overlapping each other or the mirror strip. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected piece; SPACE cycles selection between the two pieces and the mirror. RULE: Only the currently selected piece moves, identified by its active highlight color changing to match the target beneath it. TRAP: Assuming all dots remain white when active; they turn yellow when over a target, confusing selection logic if you only look for white markers.

GOAL: Fill the grid with purple, orange, and white triangles meeting perfectly along the diagonal. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate your stamp angle, mouse clicks select the color, and space applies the stamp. RULE: Each stamp covers a triangular half-grid, so opposite angles must be used to fill complementary corners. TRAP: Assuming one stamp covers the whole side; overlapping opposite stamps overwrites the first, requiring careful layering.

GOAL: Align colored plugs with matching bands by raising plug levels. CONTROLS: Click left button to shift plug up one step in its column. RULE: Each click raises a plug; stop when plug matches band color and height. TRAP: Clicking right lowers the plug, undoing progress and wasting moves.

GOAL: Position the mirror correctly so reflections align pieces with their yellow targets. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active object; Space cycles selection between the mirror and pieces. RULE: Mirrors reflect pieces across their axis, allowing alignment via indirect paths rather than direct movement. TRAP: Assuming mirrors block pieces. They pass over them, so do not waste moves trying to avoid overlaps.

GOAL: Move the piece along diagonal dots to reach the moon. CONTROLS: Click any dot within three steps to slide the piece there instantly. RULE: The piece moves exactly to the clicked dot, consuming only one action regardless of distance. TRAP: Thinking you must click every single dot; this wastes actions when you can jump multiple steps.

GOAL: Drop the magenta block into the floor notch by positioning the blue platform beneath it. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the blue platform horizontally; Space releases the falling block. RULE: The block lands on the platform and rests there, allowing you to carry it to the target. TRAP: Believing arrows move the falling block directly; they only control the platform that catches it.

GOAL: Align seven shifting keys to match the target pattern by cycling through shapes. CONTROLS: Left and right arrows move the cursor between slots; up and down arrows cycle the current key forward or backward. RULE: Keys wrap in a fixed seven-step loop, so choose the shorter path to save moves. TRAP: Forgetting that the sequence cycles means pressing the wrong direction wastes actions instead of reaching the target efficiently.

GOAL: Fill four middle slots with colors matching the top legend's order. CONTROLS: Click a bottom color to select it, then click a middle slot to place it. RULE: Placement consumes the palette square, replacing it with a gray dot. TRAP: Assuming clicks only select; ignoring the necessary second click to place causes no progress.

GOAL: Decode yellow glyphs to target blue shapes in seven slots. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the cursor; up and down cycled through shape options. RULE: Each yellow symbol mapped to a specific blue shape based on left-to-right order. TRAP: Assuming duplicate yellow pairs produced identical outputs; they mapped to different distinct shapes.

GOAL: Trace glyph shapes through two linked transformation tables to derive the final output row. CONTROLS: Arrow keys navigate slots; other keys select the correct glyph shape for each position. RULE: Each output shape serves as the input for the next step, forming a strict sky-to-pink-to-yellow chain. TRAP: Assuming slots match by position rather than value; verify each intermediate shape exists in the second table.

GOAL: Combine two small pieces into a large letter to deliver to the moon. CONTROLS: Click a grid cell to move your character toward that spot. RULE: Pieces merge automatically when they land within three squares of each other. TRAP: Believing you must land directly on the target piece; precise adjacent placement triggers the merge instead.

GOAL: Move two crosses to specific centers to overlap dots of matching colors. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the active cross; Space switches control between the yellow and blue crosses. RULE: Each arrow press moves the cross three spaces, requiring precise counting to reach exact targets. TRAP: Assuming arrows control both crosses simultaneously wastes moves; you must explicitly switch focus with Space.

GOAL: Pass the string through the ring's empty center while keeping the bead clear of the hole. CONTROLS: Click endpoints to stretch the string across the grid. RULE: Only the string passing through the ring counts; placing the star or bead there fails. TRAP: Assuming the star or bead needed to sit inside the ring hole wasted your first attempts.

GOAL: Match colored tiles to hidden legend slots. CONTROLS: Click to swap tiles, Space to verify. RULE: Tiles must match legend colors in left-to-right order. TRAP: Assuming every slot needs a tile; one slot can remain empty if its legend color is blocked.

GOAL: Move three shapes to cover all colored dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move shapes; Space switches shapes. RULE: Shapes must fully cover dot cells; outlines can overlap. TRAP: Thinking dots vanish when covered; they persist under shape edges.

GOAL: Fill every slot in the parent and child boxes with the correct color tiles. CONTROLS: Click a color from the bottom strip, then click an empty box slot to place it. RULE: Tiles must match the outline color of their specific box; order flows left to right. TRAP: Assuming tiles must match the connector color rather than the box outline color.

ESTABLISHED: Head moves vertically; extending wire hooks blocks against walls. Dragging down moves hooked blocks; retracting wire pushes blocks left. Green block is fixed at target row. FAILED: Moving head without hooking does not shift blocks. Dragging down does not move unhooked rack. GOAL IS NOT: Simply aligning head with target row or leaving blocks in original columns. CONTROLS: UP/DOWN moves head. RIGHT extends wire to hook. LEFT retracts wire, pushing hooked block sideways.

GOAL: Extend the green bar until it covers the central plus sign. CONTROLS: Click the right side of the green panel to lengthen the bar. RULE: The level completes when the bar overlaps the target zone, not when it stops precisely on it. TRAP: Believing the bar must align perfectly with the center; overshooting is allowed and necessary.

ESTABLISHED: The plug’s tip shrinks when the grid is cleared, suggesting it acts as an energy meter. FAILED: Clicking cells to light them did not clear the level and instead drained the tip’s charge. GOAL IS NOT: Simply lighting all grid cells or rotating the plug to match a pattern. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate the plug; clicking grid cells toggles their state and consumes tip energy.

GOAL: Align three scattered shapes onto their matching colored outlines. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active shape; Space cycles selection to the next shape. RULE: Only the shape indicated by the cursor responds to arrow keys. TRAP: Assuming Space moves the shape; it only changes which shape is active, wasting moves if pressed too often.

GOAL: Move each dot to the opposite colored side of the split board. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move both dots simultaneously, with one direction mirrored. RULE: Dots cannot occupy the same cell, preventing direct overlap during swaps. TRAP: Assuming dots can pass through each other wastes time on impossible overlaps.

GOAL: The goal was to move the glowing tip leftward until it touched the head. CONTROLS: The arrow keys moved the tip. Clicking the plus cells triggered a pulse. RULE: The tip’s size oscillates during pulses, but only the arrow keys actually change its position. TRAP: I wasted time thinking pulses advanced progress. They are just animations; only movement matters.

GOAL: Shrink the plug tip to navigate the narrow cable and insert it into the head. CONTROLS: Clicks light grid cells to trigger pulses; arrows move or rotate the plug tip. RULE: Lighting the specific white pattern causes a pulse that reduces the tip's size, allowing it to pass through the neck. TRAP: Believing the plug can pass the narrow section while full-sized, causing wasted movement attempts before shrinking it.

GOAL: Place the yellow block into the yellow bracket slot. CONTROLS: Click the red arrow to rotate the ring forward; click the green arrow to rotate it backward. RULE: The ring shifts as a single unit, so every block moves simultaneously when you rotate. TRAP: Thinking you could move individual blocks; only whole-ring rotations work, so wasted clicks on specific blocks failed.

GOAL: Carry specific pegs to matching knots to complete the purple and orange rings. CONTROLS: Click a body to swap its position and carried item with another body. RULE: The ring only closes when the correct peg type reaches its corresponding knot. TRAP: Assuming the knot snaps to the nearest integer coordinate rather than the exact centroid.

GOAL: Extend four colored segments to form a continuous path connecting specific start points to a target dot. CONTROLS: Click each segment to extend its length by a fixed increment, shifting the chain’s position. RULE: Segments grow sequentially, pushing subsequent segments forward; all parts must stay within open space. TRAP: Assuming you can click any segment freely; order matters because early growth can block later extensions if walls are near.

ESTABLISHED: Covering the cross rotates the legend; position matters for the win. FAILED: Matching the legend while the block sits on the cross does not win. GOAL IS NOT: Simply aligning the legend rotation anywhere on the board. CONTROLS: Movement shifts the block; covering specific tiles rotates the legend state.

GOAL: Guide both squares to cross paths in the center without colliding or touching danger zones. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move both squares simultaneously in the same direction; walls block movement, keeping a square in place. RULE: A square moves only if its destination is fully walkable; landing on red bands causes immediate failure. TRAP: Treating red danger zones as impassable walls rather than lethal traps that kill the square upon entry.

GOAL: Move the block to the marked box. CONTROLS: Arrow keys push the block one step. RULE: The block must align with the target marker. TRAP: Ignoring the block's fixed orientation while rotating the legend wastes time; the block’s color pattern never changes.

GOAL: Clear the board by reducing pegs to one. CONTROLS: Click a peg to charge it, then click the highlighted landing spot to jump. RULE: A peg must jump over an adjacent neighbor into an empty space to remove it. TRAP: Clicking a non-charged peg cancels the current move instead of starting a new jump.

GOAL: You solved a knot puzzle by moving pegs to reshape tangled loops into specific target shapes. CONTROLS: Click a peg to pick it up, then click a destination to move it; clicking another peg swaps them. RULE: The knot’s position updates dynamically based on the geometric center of all currently placed pegs. TRAP: Assuming pegs must move in a fixed sequence; ignoring the shared center point led to invalid intermediate knot positions.

GOAL: Align two yellow markers into their target slots on the rotating rings. CONTROLS: Click left or right arrows to rotate specific ring layers clockwise or counter-clockwise. RULE: Rotating a ring shifts all items on that layer one step in the chosen direction. TRAP: Assuming arrows move single items rather than the entire ring layer leads to misalignment.

GOAL: Move the yellow and orange blocks into their matching outer brackets. CONTROLS: Click red or green arrows to rotate the left and right rings clockwise or counter-clockwise. RULE: The rings share two middle cells, allowing blocks to switch tracks only when aligned. TRAP: Assuming the rings are independent; ignoring the shared cells makes the puzzle impossible.

GOAL: Make the boxed panel's color pattern match the static mini-map target. CONTROLS: Clicking a colored cell toggles it between red and blue. RULE: The mini-map is a fixed goal, not a live reflection of the panel's current state. TRAP: Assuming the mini-map updates with the panel; it stayed static, revealing the true target.

GOAL: Turn specific grid cells red to match the hidden patterns shown in two small maps. CONTROLS: Click a blue cell to flip it to red; click again to revert. RULE: White dots on a mini-map mean the corresponding cell must be red; gray means blue. TRAP: Assuming the orange center dot changes the color rule; it is just a visual marker, not a new target color.

GOAL: Align the plug's prongs with the socket's tabs to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the plug; Space rotates it to change orientation. RULE: The plug's prongs must slide directly into the socket's empty slots. TRAP: Assuming the socket moves; only the plug responds to arrow inputs.

GOAL: Align all colored tokens by rotating rows and columns to form matching patterns. CONTROLS: Click horizontal or vertical axes to rotate entire rows or columns left/right or up/down. RULE: Every rotation shifts all tokens in that line by one position, cycling edge tokens to the opposite side. TRAP: Assuming tokens stay in their original row; they jump between rows when rotated, breaking previous alignments.

GOAL: Reveal the hidden shape by turning cells to match the target pattern. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell toggles its color between red and orange. RULE: White pixels in mini-maps mean the cell matches the mini-map center's color; gray means it matches the other color. TRAP: Assuming mini-map colors directly show cell colors, rather than using the center as a reference key.

ESTABLISHED: A central wall blocks the corridor. Two plates exist, one left, one right. Merging boxes is possible. The right plate is reachable if the wall opens. FAILED: Placing a single box on the left plate did not open the wall. Pushing a corridor box right remained a no-op. GOAL IS NOT: Simply covering the left plate with one box to trigger the door. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active piece. A specific button merges adjacent pieces into a larger block. Another button splits them.

ESTABLISHED: The red object is a single connected component containing an emitter, wire, and receiver. The player moves on a lattice. FAILED: Moving into the emitter's cell from the left produced no shift or change. Standard movement into blocked cells does nothing. GOAL IS NOT: Simply walking to the target or pushing the entire red assembly as a rigid block. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player. SPACE resets the run. No other inputs have shown effect.

GOAL: Move two mirrored pieces to overlap perfectly on the central axis. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved both pieces simultaneously in the same direction. RULE: The pieces are exact mirror images; moving one moves the other symmetrically. TRAP: Believing pieces block each other; they pass through and overlap to form the target shape.

GOAL: Match all mini-maps to their center color, with gray cells always turning Red. CONTROLS: Click a cell to cycle its color Blue to Red to Orange and back to Blue. RULE: White markers indicate the cell takes the mini-map's center color, while gray markers force Red. TRAP: Assuming gray cells stay unchanged; they actually require one click to become Red, unlike white cells needing two clicks to reach Orange.

GOAL: Align green and blue pieces to mate with static pins. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move active piece; mouse clicks select new piece. RULE: Pieces move in large fixed steps, ignoring overlaps with other pieces. TRAP: Mistaking the shrinking bar for a strict action limit, causing hesitation.

GOAL: Solve the puzzle by moving the active block to the target plate. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active block; clicking a block makes it active. RULE: Pushing a merged pair launches the front block through purple walls. TRAP: Assuming blocks stay together; the front one teleports, leaving the other behind.

GOAL: Align the black piece and mirror line so their dotted patterns match perfectly. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the currently active object. Space switched control between the line and the piece. RULE: Whichever object has white dots is the one you control with arrows; the other has blue dots. TRAP: Assuming arrows always moved the piece; you must press space to select it before moving.

GOAL: Guide the green block through the colored maze to the exit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block; clicking sockets toggles wall orientations. RULE: Red and dark red cells are passable, allowing passage through solid-looking barriers. TRAP: Assuming dark red blocks movement, causing hesitation and wasted actions instead of moving through.

GOAL: Place two large blocks into the frame's empty slots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player; Space grabs or drops the held block. RULE: You must stand directly beneath a block to lift it, and stand directly beneath the target spot to drop it. TRAP: Moving sideways while carrying a block shifts the block's position relative to the drop zone, requiring careful alignment before releasing.

GOAL: Align the plug's tip with the yellow socket by positioning the blocks correctly. CONTROLS: The top blue button shifts the upper block left and lower block right; the bottom blue button moves the plug right. RULE: The blocks act as a mechanical linkage, moving in opposite directions to create a shear effect that guides the plug. TRAP: Assuming the gray area is a single rigid object; it is actually two independent pieces that slide apart to reveal the path.

ESTABLISHED: Water connects the top pool to the bubble's chamber via a cleared left channel. Two bricks block the ceiling near this channel. The bubble sits in the lower right pool. FAILED: Removing lower bricks created water flow but did not move the bubble. The bubble remains stationary despite the connection. GOAL IS NOT: Simply draining water or removing all bricks. CONTROLS: LEFT moves the bubble six columns. Clicking removes specific bricks.

GOAL: Move two shapes onto yellow targets. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected shape. Space switches the active shape. RULE: Only one shape moves at a time; the other stays still. TRAP: Moving the background line first wastes actions if it does not block the shapes.

GOAL: Slide the green plug right until its tip aligns with the socket at column 28. CONTROLS: Click below the right bar to push the plug right; click below the left bar to clear gray from the middle zone. RULE: The plug only moves if the middle zone has space, so you must alternate clearing gray and pushing. TRAP: Believing you could push the plug repeatedly without first removing gray from the path caused blocked actions.
GOAL: Clear the ceiling to reach the surface. CONTROLS: Arrows move; clicks break blocks. RULE: Break one block to open a rising path. TRAP: Moving before clearing the path wastes turns.

ESTABLISHED: The preview shows white on top and purple below. The container is a triangular grid, not a rectangular block. FAILED: Filling the entire container purple or matching the preview's row-by-row layout produced zero score. GOAL IS NOT: A simple top-half white, bottom-half purple split or a full purple fill. CONTROLS: Swatches change the claw's cup color; tilting and pouring move liquid; the cup sits above the container.

GOAL: Assemble a letter A by positioning three separate shapes into their correct overlapping slots. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active piece; Space cycles selection to the next shape. RULE: Pieces must overlap exactly where the target silhouette requires, rather than fitting together like a jigsaw. TRAP: Assuming pieces cannot occupy the same space leads to wasted moves trying to avoid necessary intersections.

GOAL: Make every grid cell match its target color while keeping special mini-maps intact. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell flips its color and updates its neighbors. RULE: Checkers must be clicked once to fix their color; plain cells need one click if they mismatch. TRAP: Assuming clicking a checker ignores mini-map constraints, or forgetting that mini-map rules dictate specific checker colors.

GOAL: Reach the exit corner using the fewest moves. CONTROLS: Arrows move you two tiles, requiring both the intermediate and destination tiles to be open. RULE: You never move one tile; blocked second tiles cause no movement, not a shortened step. TRAP: Assuming you can slide one tile when a wall blocks the second spot wastes time; plan paths where every two-tile step is fully clear.

GOAL: Match specific water levels in tanks A, D, and E while ignoring B and C. CONTROLS: Clicking a pipe segment moves two units of water from the left tank to the right tank. RULE: Water only flows if the source level exceeds the wall height and the destination stays within bounds. TRAP: Assuming clicks adjust levels by one unit causes miscounting, as each action shifts exactly two units.

GOAL: Guide the purple square along the dotted path to clear the level. CONTROLS: Click any dot on the path to slide the square to that spot. RULE: The square moves only along the line of dots, stopping exactly where clicked. TRAP: Thinking the white plus is a destination; it was just a marker for the current limit.

GOAL: Move the falling block to a target by positioning a horizontal bar to catch it. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide the bar; Space drops the block. RULE: The block stops instantly when it lands on the bar, freezing its position. TRAP: Believing the block bounces or slides off; it actually halts completely upon contact.

GOAL: Match the top color sequence by filling the four middle slots in order. CONTROLS: Click a bottom color to select it, then click a middle slot to place it. RULE: You must pick from the palette before filling; the slot stays empty until both clicks happen. TRAP: Believing you could click slots directly to cycle colors, or that one click would both select and place.

GOAL: Align five toggles so both bar and stem are black, then click the ball to drop the plug into the socket. CONTROLS: Click toggles to cycle bar/stem colors; click the ball to run the mechanism. RULE: The plug descends one cell only when a toggle’s bar and stem are both black. TRAP: Matching gray colors do not trigger descent; only double-black states count.

GOAL: Reach the far exit while avoiding the lunging red hazard. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one tile at a time. RULE: The red enemy lunges two tiles toward you only when you end your move in its row within two tiles. TRAP: Assuming safety when adjacent; moving into the red’s row within range triggers a fatal lunge before you can react.

GOAL: Align five pink shapes to match the blue shapes directly above them. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the selection cursor; Enter selected a shape from the pool to fill the current slot. RULE: Match the geometric shape identity, ignoring rotation or color, to the blue glyph in the same column. TRAP: Assuming a complex cipher or permutation existed; simple visual shape matching was the only requirement.

GOAL: Eliminate the red sentinels by stepping onto them while navigating the grid. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one space in the chosen direction. RULE: Sentinels lunge two spaces along their facing axis, killing you if you occupy the destination. TRAP: Assuming a sentinel facing a zero-indexed edge has no range; it still lunges inward and is deadly.

GOAL: Match the target pattern by selecting glyphs from the pool into seven answer slots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; UP cycles the glyph in the selected slot. RULE: The target sequence follows the specific order of the colored pairs shown at the top. TRAP: Assuming exact pixel matches are required; shape recognition is often necessary when pixels differ slightly.

GOAL: Guide two glowing dots into matching plus signs on opposite panels. CONTROLS: Click side glyphs to extend bars horizontally or vertically in fixed steps. RULE: Each click advances the bar exactly three units toward the target socket. TRAP: Assuming free movement; ignoring the fixed three-unit step size causes overshooting and wasted actions.

GOAL: Align both colored crosses so their arms cover all target dots simultaneously. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active cross; Spacebar switches between the yellow and blue crosses. RULE: Each cross moves by a fixed step size per press, requiring exact alignment with dot coordinates. TRAP: Believing edge walls block movement when arms extend off-board; clipping is allowed, so don’t stop early.

GOAL: Arrange colored rings to match the target sequence hidden in the flashing pattern. CONTROLS: Click to select a ring, click another to swap positions, press space to scan and verify the order. RULE: The scan checks slots in a fixed order: reds first, then greens. TRAP: Assuming the scan order is random or strictly left-to-right across all colors, which led to incorrect swap planning.

GOAL: Align seven blue glyphs to match a target sequence derived from five source pairs. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor and cycle glyph choices; UP rotates the current slot’s options. RULE: Match by shape first, then exact color, prioritizing unique segmentations from the yellow sources.
